title: Exchange Rates
short: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another; a currency appreciates when it buys more of the other.
trouble: Students read a rise in yen per dollar as the yen appreciating. It means the dollar has appreciated and the yen has depreciated.

blocks.html: To buy something from another country, you usually need its currency. An exchange rate is just a price, and converting between currencies is a proportion.

An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another, such as 0.90 euros per dollar. Always read the units. If the number of euros per dollar rises, each dollar buys more euros: the dollar has appreciated and the euro has depreciated. The two ways of quoting are reciprocals: 0.90 euros per dollar is about 1.11 dollars per euro.

"Euros per dollar" is the price of a dollar, in euros. When that price goes up, the dollar is worth more: it appreciated. The same move, seen from the other side, makes the euro cheaper in dollars. Converting is unit cancelling: $\$200 \times 0.90 \dfrac{\text{euros}}{\text{dollar}} = 180$ euros. Mixing up which currency is "per" is the most common error, so write the units every time.

blocks.name: ec-forex
blocks.cap: The market for dollars (price in euros per dollar) and the mirror market for euros (price in dollars per euro). Use the converter, and notice that the two prices are always reciprocals.

blocks.title: Converting
blocks.q: The rate is 150 yen per dollar. How many yen do you get for \$40? How many dollars for 3,000 yen?

blocks.title: Which currency appreciated?
blocks.q: The rate moves from 140 to 150 yen per dollar.
steps: A dollar now buys more yen: the dollar appreciated.
A yen now buys fewer dollars ($\dfrac{1}{150}$ instead of $\dfrac{1}{140}$): the yen depreciated.

blocks.title: Percent changes
blocks.q: The rate goes from 100 to 125 yen per dollar. By what percent did each currency change?
steps: Yen: from $\dfrac{1}{100}$ to $\dfrac{1}{125}$ dollars, a change of $\dfrac{100}{125} - 1 = -20\%$, a 20% depreciation. The two changes are not the same size.

blocks.html: Reading a rise in yen per dollar as the yen appreciating. It means the dollar has appreciated and the yen has depreciated. Check: ask "how much does one dollar buy now?" More means a stronger dollar.
